scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

F-01.statement: Field route completion for manual meter reads was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep 2026, affecting 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Billing-db shows 1240 disputed bills with read_type ESTIMATED and 1785 with read_type ACTUAL.

F-03.statement: Billing-db tariff_change_log returns 0 records, indicating no tariff rate change was logged around the dispute-surge period.

F-04.statement: CRM dispute response times over 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-05.statement: CRM dispute_volume_monthly: 610 (Jun-2026), 590 (Jul-2026), 1180 (Aug-2026), 1260 (Sep-2026), i.e. an abrupt ~2x step increase starting in August.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: Dispute volume doubled mainly because ticket response/handling is slow or inadequate, not because bills are actually wrong; an auto-answer agent would resolve it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules (e.g. estimate-substitution logic) around August introduced systematic wrong bills, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-MDMS-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery to billing (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded or failed since August, forcing more estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reads (H-FIELD-BILL) were missed or late due to field staffing/route issues, increasing estimate substitution and bill errors.

H-LEGITIMATE-USAGE-SPIKE.statement: Bills are substantively accurate but reflect a legitimate seasonal usage increase (e.g. summer consumption) that customers perceive as wrong, inflating disputes without any underlying defect.

H-TARIFF-RATE-ERROR.statement: A tariff/rate calculation issue (not estimate substitution) is producing incorrect ACTUAL-read bills, driving the majority of disputes.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Route-log shows field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 at 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. a measurable shortfall in completed manual meter reads during the dispute-surge period.

Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL (billing-db, E-02): the majority (~59%) of disputed bills are on ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads, so estimate substitution (the mechanism behind the AMI/MDMS and field-read-failure hypotheses) can explain at most a minority of the dispute volume. Something else must be driving most disputes on bills that used an actual meter read.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log holds zero records (E-03), showing no tariff/rate change was logged around August-September, which weakens the premise that a tariff/rate-calculation change is driving the majority of disputes on ACTUAL-read bills.

CRM dispute response-time data (E-04) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. ticket handling is comfortably within SLA, not slow or inadequate. This undercuts the premise that response speed/handling is the driver of the dispute surge.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead), a non-authoritative stakeholder claim, states no tariff change occurred this year; this aligns directionally with E-03's authoritative billing-db log showing zero tariff changes recorded Aug-Sep 2026, but adds no new verified data and does not address why ACTUAL-read bills are disputed.

CRM dispute_volume_monthly (E-06) shows 610 tickets in Jun-2026, 590 in Jul-2026, 1180 in Aug-2026, 1260 in Sep-2026: an abrupt, near-exact 2x step increase occurring precisely at the August boundary, confirming the magnitude and sharp onset timing of the surge CL-01 describes.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) attributes late manual-read routes to being short three readers since July, which they say causes estimated bills for affected customers. This is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim offering a causal mechanism consistent with E-01's measured route-completion shortfall, but it does not address why most disputed bills (E-02) are on ACTUAL, not estimated, reads.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the utility may request field route priority changes but execution requires Field Operations Manager confirmation, reaffirming the K-DISPATCH authority structure. It is a process/authority document, not evidence about the billing dispute root cause.

symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026), with the step occurring precisely at the August boundary (E-06).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) are on accounts with ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED ones (E-02), so estimate-substitution mechanisms cannot explain most disputes.
Field manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep 2026 (E-01), affecting 9200 accounts, but this cannot be the majority cause given E-02.
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume abruptly doubled at the August 2026 boundary (E-06), and the majority (59%, 1785/3025) of disputed bills occurred on accounts with ACTUAL, non-estimated meter reads (E-02), which rules out field-read shortfalls (E-01, E-07) and AMI/MDMS delivery failure as the majority driver. The best-supported remaining mechanism is that a change to the billing import validation rules around August 2026 is producing incorrect bills on ACTUAL-read accounts (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE), which then triggers the dispute surge.

proposal.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume abruptly doubled at the August 2026 boundary (E-06), and the majority (59%, 1785/3025) of disputed bills occurred on accounts with ACTUAL, non-estimated meter reads (E-02), which rules out field-read shortfalls (E-01, E-07) and AMI/MDMS delivery failure as the majority driver. The best-supported remaining mechanism is that a change to the billing import validation rules around August 2026 is producing incorrect bills on ACTUAL-read accounts (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE), which then triggers the dispute surge.
proposal.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01, SH-CS), including implicit automated bill correction.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026), with the step occurring precisely at the August boundary (E-06).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) are on accounts with ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED ones (E-02), so estimate-substitution mechanisms cannot explain most disputes.
Field manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep 2026 (E-01), affecting 9200 accounts, but this cannot be the majority cause given E-02.
causal_chain: Around August 2026, the billing import validation logic that turns accepted meter reads into bills appears to have changed or malfunctioned (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE), consistent with estimate-substitution mechanisms being ruled out as the majority cause.
This produces incorrect bills on accounts that had ACTUAL, non-estimated reads (E-02: 1785 of 3025 disputed bills, 59%).
Incorrect bills are issued to customers in the 'bill issue' step of the meter-to-cash process.
Customers file dispute tickets at roughly double the pre-August baseline rate, starting precisely in August 2026 (E-06: 610, 590, 1180, 1260).
Ticket-handling capacity is not the bottleneck (E-04: median 1.6d / p90 2.8d within the 3.0d SLA), confirming the surge reflects upstream billing errors rather than response-time inadequacy.

assumptions.statement: A billing import validation rule change occurred near August 2026, even though the billing-config rule-change log has not yet been queried to directly confirm it.
